findings.issue: `Array.isArray(value)` is redundant: an array has no own `granted` property, so the `typeof granted === 'boolean'` check already returns null for it.
findings.evidence: if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) return null;
findings.fix: Drop `|| Array.isArray(value)`; the [true]/[] cases in the tests still pass.

findings.issue: The extra test 'parsePersistentStorage accepts only { granted: boolean }' isn't named in the spec. It mostly repeats the invalid-record loop in SPEC-08 (through readPersistentStorage) and adds to the 693-line total, which is over the 520-line budget.
findings.evidence: SPEC-08 already loops over [{granted:'yes'},{granted:1},{},null,[true],'granted',true] via readPersistentStorage; the parse test repeats almost the same set directly.
findings.fix: Remove the separate parse test, or fold its one distinctive case ({ granted: false, extra: 1 } -> false) into the SPEC-08 loop.

findings.issue: When the get request fails, storedRecord rejects without closing the database connection. An open connection can block a later version upgrade in the same page.
findings.fix: Call db.close() before reject in request.onerror.

summary: All 11 SPEC items are implemented as specified. The v5 step is additive (`if (oldVersion < 5) createObjectStore('meta')`, no record), and all three e2e/support/hand-records.ts helpers repeat it exactly at version 5. requestPersistenceOnce reads once and skips persist when a valid record exists. It calls persist only after a successful read that returns null, stores `=== true`, catches both rejections and synchronous throws, and logs the A-2/A-3 messages and resolves null instead of rejecting. main.tsx calls it once at module level after render() and does not await it, and nothing synchronous in that line can throw. browserPersist calls storage.persist() as a method. The locked edits (session-end.acceptance, home-control, opponent-styles) only re-pin 4->5 and add 'meta' to the store lists plus their comments, with every check kept. dist contains no test stub (only the real browserPersist code). Mutations are caught: persist on every launch (unit rows 5/6 plus the second-launch block, e2e SPEC-04); truthy instead of === true (unit row answer('granted') -> false); a detached call (unit this-check, e2e SPEC-01 'real' mode would record null); a missing main.tsx wiring (e2e awaitRecord poll). I re-ran the unit file and the persistent-storage, home-control and opponent-styles e2e specs on Chromium and WebKit: 25 passed, 1 skipped as intended (SPEC-01 on WebKit). Scope: 693 vs 520 lines (warn, under the 1040 fail). The extra lines are the table-driven unit test, the v4 seeding fixture and the 166-line e2e spec. That is justified, apart from a small duplicated parse test. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
